title: Claude model overview — Opus 4, Sonnet 4, Haiku 4
raw_content: Claude is available in three model tiers. Claude Opus 4 is the most capable model, excelling at complex reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks. It supports a 200K token context window and extended thinking. Claude Sonnet 4 balances performance and speed, ideal for most production workloads. Claude Haiku 4 is the fastest and most cost-effective option for lightweight tasks. All models support tool use, vision, and structured output via JSON mode.
summary: Overview of Claude 4 model family: Opus 4 (most capable), Sonnet 4 (balanced), Haiku 4 (fast/cheap). All support tool use, vision, JSON mode, and 200K context.

title: Tool use (function calling) — Building with Claude
raw_content: Claude can interact with external tools and APIs through tool use (also called function calling). You define tools with a name, description, and JSON Schema for parameters. Claude decides when to call a tool, generates the required arguments, and you execute the tool server-side, returning results in a tool_result block. Best practices: provide clear tool descriptions, use specific parameter schemas, handle errors gracefully, and limit the number of tools to under 20 for optimal performance. Claude supports parallel tool calls when multiple independent tools are needed.
summary: Guide to Claude tool use / function calling. Define tools with JSON Schema, Claude generates arguments, you execute server-side. Supports parallel tool calls. Keep under 20 tools for best results.

title: Extended thinking is now generally available
raw_content: Extended thinking is now generally available for Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4. When enabled, Claude produces a thinking block before its response, showing its step-by-step reasoning. This improves performance on complex math, code analysis, and multi-step planning tasks. Set the budget_tokens parameter to control how many tokens Claude can use for thinking (minimum 1024, maximum 128000). Extended thinking is billed at standard output token rates. The thinking block is returned as a separate content block with type 'thinking'.
summary: Extended thinking GA for Opus 4 and Sonnet 4. Produces visible reasoning steps. budget_tokens controls thinking length (1024-128000). Billed as output tokens.

title: Prompt caching — Reduce latency and costs
raw_content: Prompt caching allows you to cache frequently used context between API calls, reducing latency by up to 85% and costs by up to 90% on cache hits. Mark cacheable content with cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' } on system prompts, tool definitions, or user message prefixes. Cached content has a 5-minute TTL that refreshes on each cache hit. Minimum cacheable prefix length is 1024 tokens for Sonnet and Opus, 2048 tokens for Haiku. Cache write tokens cost 25% more than standard input tokens; cache read tokens cost 10% of standard input tokens.
summary: Prompt caching reduces latency 85% and costs 90% on cache hits. Use cache_control ephemeral markers. 5-min TTL refreshes on hit. Min prefix: 1024 tokens (Sonnet/Opus), 2048 (Haiku).
